first.rationale: The immediate competitive threat is concentrated in price-sensitive SMB accounts, and inherited evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing produced strong acquisition and revenue lift in that segment. I would verify both the pricing result and the onboarding evidence before committing because activation and onboarding are simultaneously declining. A targeted, time-bounded test is preferable to a broad discount because margin, retention, and customer-quality effects remain uncertain.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the onboarding flow. Verified evidence shows shorter onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing the current 4% completion decline and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly judged unsuitable for sustainable growth.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment for this cycle. Its verified results improved completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%), directly addressing current funnel deterioration with evidence of sustainable value. The deeper competitive cut raises urgency, but switching to promotional pricing would knowingly repeat a result with 30-day retention down 12% and an explicit finding that it was not sustainable. The risk is that the SMB price threat remains insufficiently addressed this week; do not trade verified retention harm for a short-term acquisition response without new evidence.
